chapter: Serenading and playing with Buddy Bolden
title: Playing with Buddy Bolden at Kenner's Hall
summary: Garland subbed on bass for Little Jimmy at Liberty and Perdido and names Bolden's lineup: Willie Cornish, Frank Lewis, Brock Mumford and James Phillip.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Alright, we can turn it off. Tell me about, did you ever know Buddy Bolden? Did you ever hear him?
I played with Buddy Bolden.
You played with Buddy Bolden?
Right at Liberty and Perdita. Alright.
Liberty and Perdita.
At the Kennes Hall. We played there on Saturday night and Sunday morning and have church in there.
I know what you're talking about.
That line up. Buddy, I played in Little Jimmy's place. I pinched it for Jimmy.
Oh yeah.

Then the band consisted of Jimmy Adyazin on the bass. Carnish, Willie Carnish was on trombone. Frank, I forget Frank's last name, played clarinet. The guy from across the lake? And then Brock played guitar. James E. Phillip played drums. That's way back now you don't talk about.
James E. Phillip? James E. Phillip.
James E. Phillip. Played drums.
Oh, that must be Bigfoot Bill Phillip's daddy or something. Might be, did you ever know Bigfoot Bill Phillip? He's after your time, I guess.
That's after my time, no.
That's a late, late drum. I don't know.
I know his daddy. I thought he was his daddy.
Did you know Frank Lewis?
Well, Frank Lewis was the clarinet player.
Oh, I see.
With Buddy Bolden.
Yeah, I see.
I sure know him.
